priorFindingsVerification.note: Re-read lock.mjs fresh in full this session (lines 1-209). Confirmed acquire() (lines 153-158) is a single tryCreateLockFile attempt, and, only if that fails, a single reclaimStaleLock attempt (lines 128-151) -- itself a one-shot stat+isLockStale-check+atomic-rename, never a retry-with-wait loop -- returning true/false immediately either way. withGigLock (lines 187-209) returns {ok:false} immediately on failure to acquire, with 'no queueing, no waiting' (its own docstring, line 178). This confirms the corrected justification's central claim: classical hold-and-wait deadlock is structurally impossible against this primitive regardless of acquisition order, because no caller ever blocks while holding one lock and waiting for a second. Grepped both spec files for every 'deadlock' occurrence (behavioral-spec.md:89,990,999,1005,1012,1017,1020,1022,1029,1040,1358; verification-architecture.md:25,36,146) -- every remaining mention is the CORRECTED framing ('resolves FIND-501', 'NOT a deadlock-avoidance mechanism', 'this is NOT required for correctness today') with zero surviving claims that the fixed lock-acquisition order is needed to prevent deadlock. No false deadlock-avoidance claim remains anywhere in either spec file.
